habitat: Parties of six to ten in thickets in woodland, mixed bushveld and wooded hillsides, usually in the lower stratum. Newman also notes suburbia in Zimbabwe.
summary: A common resident. Dark brown above, with a grey-brown breast, a tawny belly, and whitish arrow-like streaks above and below. The eyes are orange with red eye-rings, and the bill and legs are black. The immature lacks the arrow marks and is usually seen with adults. The call is an excitable whirring, scurr-scurr-scurr, taken up by the whole party until it resembles hysterical giggling. The Kemp code RB was left unchanged.

similar.note: Green Wood Hoopoe has a more musical chatter. The babbler's scurr-scurr-scurr is more mechanical.

calls.description: An excitable whirring, started by one bird and taken up by the party until it resembles hysterical giggling. The basic sound is scurr-scurr-scurr, more mechanical than a Green Wood Hoopoe. Grade A call from Tzendse Camp in the Kruger Park, Mopani, Limpopo. The filename is XC368185-170403_Arrow-markedBabbler_TzendseCamp_OC.mp3.

research.note: Status is resident and all twelve months are listed. Newman calls it a common resident. Hartlaub’s Babbler is the plumage comparison Newman names and is not in this list. The breast is described as grey-brown, which is not a colour token, so that colour is left blank. Population figures and the Kemp code RB were left unchanged.
